title.narrative: Judicial Services and Smart Infrastructure Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Judicial Services and Smart Infrastructure Project for Azerbaijan is to improve the access, transparency, and efficiency of delivery of selected justice services. The project comprises of four components. The first component, judicial service delivery improvements will finance two sub-components: access to justice and the expansion of e-Justice services. The second component, strengthening institutional capacity, efficiency, and monitoring and evaluation will finance technical assistance, training, and advisory services to improve the capability of key justice entities to make informed policy decisions and implement reforms. There are following four sub-components: (i) improvements to justice sector performance; (ii) strengthen the information systems management and operational capability of the ministry of justice (MOJ); (iii) communications, outreach, and change management activities aimed at facilitating stakeholder engagement in justice sector reforms; and (iv) strengthen the professional capacity of judges, of staff of courts and the MOJ, and of the justice academy. The third component, expansion and modernization of justice infrastructure will finance the construction and rehabilitation of about six courthouses and court complexes at locations selected in accordance with criteria set forth in the operational manual, through the carrying out of works and the provision of goods, consultants' services, and training. The fourth component, project management and coordination will strengthen the capacity of the MOJ in project management, monitoring, and coordination including audits of: (i) project financial statements, (ii) environmental and social safeguard compliance, and (iii) implementation of information and communications technology activities under the project, all through the provision of goods, consultants' services, and training, and the financing of incremental operating costs.
The objective of the project is to improve the access, transparency and efficiency of delivery of selected justice services.

condition.narrative: Article 5.01. The Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consist of the following, namely, that the Borrower, through the JMT, hasupdated the Project Operations Manual for the purposes of this Loan, in a manner satisfactory to the Bank.

Finance Agreement: Chief information and technology officer: Section I.A.2. of Schedule 2 | Description: The Borrower, through theMOJ, shall retain a chief information and technology officer within the JMT with responsibilities acceptable to the Bank. |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Environmental Safeguards: Section C.1. of Schedule 2 | Description: The Borrower shall ensure that the Projectis carried out in accordance with the EMP and RPF, and shall ensure that all measures necessary for the carrying out of the EMP andRPF shall be taken in a timely manner. Except as the Bank shall otherwise agree, the Borrower shall not assign, amend, abrogate orwaive the EMP and/or RPF. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Environmental Safeguards: Section C.2. of Schedule 2 | Description: Prior to the commencement of works for eachproposed site, the Borrower shall ensure that: (a) the related site-specific EMPs are prepared in accordance with the EMP; (b) theproposed design and site for said works incorporate the provisions of site-specific EMPs; (c) the provisions of said site-specificEMPs are adequately included in the proposed contract for said works; and (d) such works are carried out in accordance with therespective site-specific EMPs. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Information technology department in MOJ - establishment: Section I.A.3. of Schedule 2 | Description: TheBorrower, through the MOJ, shall establish by no later than January 1, 2016 an information technology department in the MOJ, withresources and responsibilities acceptable to the Bank, and with competent staff in adequate numbers. | Due Date :01-Jan-2016

Finance Agreement: Information technology department in MOJ - maintenance: Section I.A.3. of Schedule 2 | Description: TheBorrower, through the MOJ, shall maintain an information technology department in the MOJ, with resources and responsibilitiesacceptable to the Bank, and with competent staff in adequate numbers. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Institutional arrangements: Section I.A.1. of Schedule 2 | Description: The Borrower shall vest the overallresponsibility for the implementation of the Project in the JMT and shall maintain the JMT, at all times during Projectimplementation, with resources and responsibilities acceptable to the Bank, and with competent staff in adequate numbers. TheBorrower shall ensure that the JMT shall carry out the Project in accordance with the Operational Manual and, except as the Bankshall otherwise agree, shall not amend, suspend, abrogate, repeal or waive any provision of said Manual without the prior writtenapproval of the Bank. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Finance Agreement: Social Safeguards: Section C.3. of Schedule 2 | Description: The Borrower shall ensure that the RAPs: (a) shallbe prepared in a manner satisfactory to the Bank in accordance with the RPF prior to commencement of any activities for the areaswhere physical relocation, land acquisition and/or loss of income due to the Project activities have been identified, and; (b)shall be carried out in a timely manner, satisfactory to the Bank. In the event that land acquisition or resettlement is requiredfor the purposes of carrying out activities, the Borrower shall (a) notify the Bank of any intended acquisition of land orresettlement; (b) disclose the RPF and each RAP (if any) prepared under the Project, and; (c) ensure that the MOJ causes all landacquisition and resettlement under the Project to be undertaken in accordance with the provisions and procedures contained in theRPF and the respective RAP, and that all relevant information is adequately provided to all affected persons, and potentiallyaffected persons, in a timely and adequate manner. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Improved Access: Increased access to services by different groups of users in all six court jurisdictions

comment.narrative:
This number is cumulative from January 1, 2015 until June 21, 2024.
The original target at closing (2018) was set at 70,000 beneficiaries.
Among the total of 6,385,600 project beneficiaries , including those accessing information online, a total of 4,974,467 beneficiaries was identifiable by gender, IDP states and alike. Hence, the project also met its revised closing target if the total number of beneficiaries is narrowed down to the segment of those that are identifiable.

title.narrative: Increase woman representation in the justice sector
Number of citizens benefitting from legal aid and counseling services

comment.narrative: The number is cumulative from January 1, 2015 until June 21, 2024.

title.narrative: Legal aid laws and procedures reviewed and improvements adopted

comment.narrative: The project continuously gathered and reviewed findings from project activities in the light of the existing legal framework. The project prepared suggestions for changes and amendments to existing laws which the MoJ brought forward to Parliament for discussion and approval.

title.narrative: Improved Transparency: Information on sector budget and performance available on the Supreme Court website and Unified Court Portal

comment.narrative: Five categories of information related to JSSIP-financed activities are relevant for this indicator: (1) number and value of judicial decisions enforced (MoJ) and processed (MoJ); (2) number of state registration requests received and processed (MoJ); (3) number of inspections conducted (MoJ); (4) court-level (not by individual judge) data on the number of cases received and number of cases resolved by category each year (e.g., civil, administrative and criminal (Supreme Court); and (5) results of periodic surveys of users of the justice system to assess their satisfaction with service delivery, updated each time the survey is conducted (MoJ and Supreme Curt).

title.narrative: Users expressing satisfaction with access, transparency and efficiency of selected justice services

comment.narrative:
Multi-stakeholder surveys were carried out in 2017/18, 2019/20, 2022, 2023 and 2024. The overall satisfaction rate includes all target audiences regardless of prior experience with court services; sub-indicators for satisfaction among citizens and businesses cover those with prior court experience.
The original target at closing (2018) was set at 50% overall satisfaction.
In parallel to the multi-stakeholder satisfaction surveys the project undertook complementary short and ad hoc surveys, sends out quick feedback requests regarding implementation and roll-out of specific project activities, and conducted focus group discussions with select stakeholders to inform implementation of project activities.

title.narrative: Cost Savings from Reduced Administrative and Compliance Burden of Business Inspections

comment.narrative: Changes to the law mid-implementation limited the scope of inspections conducted by government agencies. The indicator is no longer relevant. Law No. 1410-IVQ of October 20, 2015 and the Presidential Decree No. 660 of October 26, 2015 suspended the requirement to undertake business inspections; first until October 31, 2017, now extended until further notice. The project cannot track the cot implications/savings of a suspended government procedure. The indicator will no longer be tracked per the restructuring paper (October 2018) and amended results framework.

title.narrative: Audio-video court proceedings transcription system operational in e-Courts across all six court jurisdictions

comment.narrative: All courts are connected to the e-Courts since May 2023 and equipped with the audio-video court proceedings transcription system.

title.narrative: Supreme Court E-Library Information is Accessed by Users

comment.narrative: This intermediate results indicator was carried over from the parent project and tracked here for continued monitoring and sustainability of investments made.

title.narrative: MOJ IT Call Center and Help Desk operational

comment.narrative: On May May 31, 2021, the MoJ has taken over full responsibility for the IT Department and support provided to the e-Courts.

title.narrative: Justice Sector Gender Strategy and Action Plan is publicly available

comment.narrative:
The Strategy and Recommendations is available on Unified Court Web Portal:
https://courts.gov.az/en/main/page/Final-Justice-Gender-Strategy-and-Action-PLan_3224

title.narrative: Disputes processed using mediation mechanisms in select court jurisdictions in Baku, Sheki and Sumgayit
Improved Efficiency: Increased efficiency of service delivery

comment.narrative: The project finances activities to improve the delivery of services in all six court jurisdictions both in terms of timeliness as well as cost savings. The indicator is measured based on the achievements of the following indicators: - Cost savings from reduced administrative and compliance burden of business inspections - Average energy consumption in JSSIP-financed 'smart courts' - Time taken to enforce contracts - Number of uncontested civil enforcement cases electronically processed - Improved cost recovery through e-Courts

Activities under this sub-indicator entail engagement with stakeholders (MoJ, judiciary, lawyers, non-governmental organizations/legal aid providers, academia) to ensure their input and buy-in for the implementation of AI and BI in the judicial sector in Azerbaijan.

title.narrative: Number of people trained for the use of e-applications
Courts and other justice sector entitites connected to e-Courts

comment.narrative: All courts are connected to the e-Courts as of May 2023.

title.narrative: Piloting of TT prototypes for productivity and efficiency gains

comment.narrative: Six use cases for AI and BI solutions in the judiciary of relevance to Azerbaijan have been identified, a high-level implementation blueprint and high-level technical requirements for implementation (roadmap) were developed; and prototypes for four BI use cases and two AI use cases were developed.

title.narrative: Average energy consumption in JSSIP-financed 'smart courts' - kilowatt-hours per square meter per annum

comment.narrative:
All court houses and court complexes constructed under the project are operational, and hand-over procedures have been completed.
The Main Data Center (Baku) and Reserve Data Center (Yevlakh) - core elements of the e-Court system - are constructed, operational and certified by the Uptime Institute.

title.narrative: Information on construction activities is publicly accessible

comment.narrative: The MOJ arranged for live web-streaming from construction sites for smart courts as a measure of openness and transparency during the construction. The links to respective construction sites are no longer available due to completion of the court yards and removal of camera stands.

title.narrative: Global Data Management Community (DAMA International) metrics applied to at least one database
Guidelines for using transformative technologies developed, including assessment of readiness and risk mitigation capabilities
